gallery.filename: Barrow, Windmill Hill, near Winterbourne Monkton - geograph.org.uk - 1010839.jpg
gallery.title: File:Barrow, Windmill Hill, near Winterbourne Monkton - geograph.org.uk - 1010839.jpg
gallery.description: Barrow, Windmill Hill, near Winterbourne Monkton Windmill Hill was occupied about 5,500 years ago in the Neolithic period. There are signs of earthworks such as banks and ditches to be found although nowhere near as well-defined as other settlements such as Liddington and Barbury north of here in Swindon. This is a bell barrow according to the National Trust signs at the entrances to the hill. The other barrows are bowl barrows and saucer barrows. This one has a ditch around it. Beyond in the far distance can be seen the arable areas west of the Winterbournes.
categories: Images from Geograph Britain and Ireland

gallery.title: File:Bell barrow, Windmill Hill, near Winterbourne Monkton - geograph.org.uk - 1010949.jpg
gallery.description: Bell barrow, Windmill Hill, near Winterbourne Monkton. This another view of the barrow in this image 1010839 but facing north-east. This would appear to be the highest point on the hill. There are good views from up here such as 1010863 1010872 1010747 and 1010718 The land in the far distance to the right of the barrow is Hackpen Hill with its white horse over 5 kilometres away.
categories: Images from Geograph Britain and Ireland

gallery.filename: The eastern edge of Windmill Hill, near Winterbourne Monkton - geograph.org.uk - 1011020.jpg
gallery.title: File:The eastern edge of Windmill Hill, near Winterbourne Monkton - geograph.org.uk - 1011020.jpg
gallery.description: The eastern edge of Windmill Hill, near Winterbourne Monkton I'm not entirely sure of the identity of the features in the foreground. The information boards at the entrances to the hill refer to quarries and saucer barrows at this location. However, from looking at the aerial views I think these are the quarries. It would be nice sometime to visit here with someone with expert knowledge of what is here.
